title: Is it already decided?
blurb: Nothing has been chosen yet in any of these situations. That does not mean anything is still possible — in Paxos the outcome can be sealed long before anyone could know it. Which of these values could still end up being chosen?

justification.text: No. Alice can no longer be chosen, whatever happens from here. Every majority a future proposer could gather would report Bob as the highest acceptance it has seen, which forces that proposer to propose Bob rather than Alice. Nothing has been chosen yet, and no acceptor in this situation knows that, but it is already decided.
Yes. A proposer that opens a new ballot and hears from Acceptor 1 and Acceptor 2 would see Bob as the highest acceptance among them, so it would have to propose Bob, and they can accept it.

Yes, though nothing in the state above shows it. Every majority you could read off the table right now would force a new proposer to propose Alice. What keeps Bob alive is an earlier ballot that was started and never finished: its promises are still usable, and they report what those acceptors had accepted at the time, which is less than they have accepted since. One way it plays out:
steps: The proposer running ballot 3 asks every acceptor to promise ballot 3.
Acceptor 1 promises ballot 3, reporting Alice in ballot 0.
Acceptor 2 promises ballot 1, reporting that it has accepted nothing.
The proposer running ballot 1, after hearing back from Acceptor 2 and Acceptor 3, proposes Bob.
Acceptor 2 accepts Bob in ballot 1.
Acceptor 2 promises ballot 3, reporting Bob in ballot 1.
The proposer running ballot 3, after hearing back from Acceptor 1 and Acceptor 2, proposes Bob.
Acceptor 1 accepts Bob in ballot 3.
Acceptor 2 accepts Bob in ballot 3.
